plannedStops.title: Planned Stops
plannedStops.subtitle: Time deliberately set aside as non-production. Every minute here is one somebody entered.
plannedStops.noSchedules: No schedules yet. A shift or a stop needs one in order to recur.
plannedStops.name: Name
plannedStops.oneOffHelp: For a one-off day such as Friday overtime. The weekly pattern is ignored.
plannedStops.holidayHelp: A weekday you do not select is a non-working day — that is how a holiday is expressed. There is no separate holiday list to fall out of step with.
plannedStops.noStops: No planned stops. Breaks and cleaning are no longer assumed — create the ones this plant actually takes.
plannedStops.offsetHelp: When the stop begins, counted from the start of the shift. Previously the system placed the break at the midpoint and the cleaning at the end — neither was a choice anyone made.
plannedStops.startTimeHelp: The clock time the stop begins, in plant time. A stop on its own schedule has no shift to be counted from — without this there is nowhere on the day to put it, and an earlier version silently placed every one of them at midnight.
plannedStops.noStartTime: No start time — this stop produces nothing
plannedStops.scopeHelp: A break usually stops a line; cleaning one machine stops only that machine. The old behaviour applied every stop to every machine, inventing downtime for equipment nobody had touched.
plannedStops.noTargetWarn: With nothing selected this stop produces no events.
plannedStops.untargetedTitle: {{count}} planned stop(s) have no target yet
plannedStops.untargetedBody: These were migrated from the old break and cleaning settings. They produce nothing until you choose which line or machines they apply to — carrying the old "every machine" behaviour forward would have carried the defect with it.
plannedStops.notScheduled: Produced nothing (no schedule or no target): {{list}}
plannedStops.noWoRules: No rules. Changeover is not booked automatically until one exists.
plannedStops.triggerHelp_PRODUCT_CHANGE: Fires only when the SKU differs from the previous order on that machine. A cold start does not fire it — there is nothing to change from.
plannedStops.triggerHelp_ORDER_CHANGE: Fires for any new order, including another order of the same product.
plannedStops.triggerHelp_ALWAYS: Fires on every order without condition.
plannedStops.chargedHelp: Changeover is planned but still a loss in most plants, so this is on by default — the opposite of a break. Turn it off only if this plant genuinely does not count it.
plannedStops.deleteScheduleDesc: Anything still using it would stop recurring, so it is refused while a shift template points at it.
plannedStops.deleteStopDesc: Events already created keep their place in history — deleting a stop must not rewrite a month you have already reported on.
plannedStops.deleteWoDesc: The rule stops firing on future orders. Past events are kept.

machineStatus.title: Machine Status
machineStatus.subtitle: Availability, performance and quality over the selected scope and window
machineStatus.timelineHelp: One band per period a machine spent in a state. Gaps mean the machine reported nothing — they are left blank rather than filled in, because a guess here would hide a signal outage.
machineStatus.noRecords: No state records in this window
machineStatus.noMachines: No machines in the selected scope
machineStatus.noStops: No downtime recorded in this window
machineStatus.noSnapshots: No production snapshots in this window
machineStatus.paretoHelp: Blue is planned, amber is caused outside the machine, red is the machine’s own fault.
machineStatus.saturatedTitle: {{count}} machine(s) are producing at or above their ideal rate
machineStatus.saturatedBody: Performance is capped at 100% because exceeding the ideal means the ideal cycle time is wrong, not that the machine beat physics. Until the routing cycle times are corrected, this indicator carries no information for those machines — raised with the plant as tracker item 27.
machineStatus.unitHelp: Quantities are in the product’s smallest packaging unit, so machines at different stages of the line can be compared directly.
machineStatus.loadFailed: Could not load this view. The request failed — if you have just reopened the app, your session may still be waking up.
machineStatus.plannedProductionHelp: The denominator of Availability: time the machine was scheduled to produce, after planned and external stops are taken out.
machineStatus.unmeasuredHelp: Time inside a job order when the machine reported no state at all — no status signal wired, or the gateway was silent. Not counted as run or as downtime, and excluded from availability.

oeeAn.availabilitySubtitle: Where the planned production time went — and who caused each stop
oeeAn.performanceSubtitle: Pace against the ideal cycle, inside the time the machine was actually running
oeeAn.qualitySubtitle: Good units against everything the line produced
oeeAn.lossTreeSubtitle: Every minute of the calendar accounted for, from loading down to fully productive time
oeeAn.availabilitySplitHelp: Planned production time, split into what ran and what did not. Starvation and blockage are shown separately because they are not the machine's fault and are not charged to its availability.
oeeAn.worstHelp: Lowest first — the machine to look at is at the top.
oeeAn.externalNote: Starved and blocked minutes are recorded so the constraint is visible, but removed from planned production time before availability is derived. A machine is not punished for waiting on the line.
oeeAn.performanceSplitHelp: Of the minutes the machine was genuinely running, how many were spent producing at the rate it is capable of.
oeeAn.cappedTitle: {{count}} machine(s) are at or above their ideal rate
oeeAn.cappedBody: Performance is capped at 100% because beating the ideal means the ideal cycle time is wrong, not that the machine outran physics. For those machines this indicator carries no information until the routing cycle times are corrected — raised with the plant as tracker item 27.
oeeAn.performanceNote: Performance is ideal time over run time. It measures pace only: a machine that is stopped contributes nothing here — that loss belongs to availability.
oeeAn.scrapByMachineHelp: Sorted by units scrapped, not by rate — a high percentage on a short run is not the biggest problem.
oeeAn.qualityDefinitionNote: Good counts only units that passed the FINAL routing step; scrap counts rejections at EVERY step. A unit thrown out at the filler is a rejection even though it never reached the wrapper.
oeeAn.unitNote: Quantities are in the product's smallest packaging unit, so machines at different stages of the line can be compared directly.
oeeAn.waterfallHelp: Each row is a subtraction from the one above it. Percentages are of calendar time.
oeeAn.biggestLossesHelp: Largest first — this is the list to act on.
oeeAn.noLosses: No losses recorded in this window
oeeAn.teepExplain: OEE measures the plant against the hours it planned to work. TEEP measures the same output against every hour that exists. The gap is capacity the company already owns and is not using — usually a larger number than anything on the shop floor.
oeeAn.lossTreeNote: OEE = fully productive ÷ planned production. TEEP = fully productive ÷ calendar. Availability, Performance and Quality here are the same figures the OEE engine reports — these pages read it rather than recomputing it.
oeeAn.fullyLoadedTitle: The plant is scheduled around the clock
oeeAn.fullyLoadedBody: Utilisation is at 100%, so every calendar hour is planned production and TEEP equals OEE. There is no idle-capacity gap to recover here — the losses below are the only ones available.
oeeAn.trendHelp: Movement over the selected window. Hover any point for the figure.
oeeAn.whereTimeWentHelp: The whole window’s planned time, divided by what it became.
oeeAn.worstMachinesHelp: Lowest first — the machine to look at is at the top.
oeeAn.attributionHelp: Red is the machine’s own fault; amber is the line stopping it. Minutes, because minutes are what somebody can act on.
oeeAn.valuesLiveNote: This page shows change and composition. For the figures as they stand right now, use Operations Now → Live Machines.
oeeAn.wherePaceLostHelp: Run time per machine, split into the minutes that earned output and the minutes that did not.
oeeAn.outputSplitHelp: The window’s whole output. Good counts the final step only; scrap counts every step.
oeeAn.qualityByMachineHelp: Lowest first. Zoomed to the band quality lives in — a 0–100 axis hides every real change.
oeeAn.oeeVsTeepHelp: OEE measures output against the hours the plant planned to work; TEEP against every hour that exists. The gap between the two bars is capacity already owned and not used.

schedCap.title: Schedule & Capacity Analytics
schedCap.subtitle: Line OEE, order attainment and designed-capacity use — with the basis behind each figure
schedCap.selectLine: Select a production line in the scope panel to see line OEE.
schedCap.basisGapTitle: The two OEE bases differ by {{gap}} points
schedCap.basisGapBody: Schedule-based availability compares run time with the time the line was SCHEDULED to run; time-based compares it with uptime plus downtime only. Neither is wrong — they answer different questions, and a large gap means a lot of scheduled time was neither running nor logged as a stop.
schedCap.overCapacityBody: Above 100% the machine produced more than its routing cycle time says is possible. That is a master-data problem, not a performance result: the rated cycle time for these machines is too slow. Correct it in the process routing.
schedCap.lineCompositionHelp: How each machine on the line contributed, and which one the basis was taken from.
schedCap.noOrders: No production orders scheduled in this period.
schedCap.overProducedNote: {{count}} order(s) produced more than scheduled. The surplus is shown but not credited — over-producing one order cannot cover a shortfall on another.
schedCap.noRouting: Not in any active routing step
schedCap.unratedNote: These machines resolve no rated capacity and therefore add nothing to the denominator: {{names}}. Assign them to an active routing step with a cycle time for a complete figure.
schedCap.windowNote: Actual units are summed from the per-minute fact store, so output and designed capacity cover exactly the same window.
schedCap.scheduleBasisNote: This page measures the order against the window it was SCHEDULED for, so time between the planned start and the actual start counts against it. Machine Status and the Availability pages measure the machine against the time it was actually asked to produce. Different questions, both from the same fact store — a lower figure here means the order started late, not that the machine ran worse.
schedCap.attainmentTrendHelp: Where each order stood at the end of each day. Derived from the per-minute fact store — the order counter itself only knows today.
schedCap.capacityTrendHelp: Daily good output against the routing’s designed throughput for those hours.

live.externalLossHelp: The line could not feed this machine, so its minutes leave the OEE denominator entirely. A breakdown would stay in it -- that is the machine's own fault.
